title: Recognizing presheaf quasi-compactness and separation from scheme charts
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $g:X\to T$ be a presheaf map. Let $(t_i:T_i\to T)_{i\in I}$ be an etale jointly surjective family of schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Suppose scheme etale charts $V_i\to X$ and maps $p_i:V_i\to T_i$ give specified cartesian squares $V_i=X\times_T T_i$. If every scheme map $p_i$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], then $g$ satisfies IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap [def-sfb-space-quasi-compact-presheaf-map] and IsSeparatedPresheafMap [def-sfb-presheaf-map-separated-diagonal]. The index universe is arbitrary.

source.place: Tags 03KG and 03KM; schemes.tex Tag 01K5 and morphisms.tex Tag 01QR; original preparation Step 7.

proof.text: For an affine test of each p_i, scheme base change is quasi-compact; since the test is affine, the source is quasi-compact. Its identity supplies a surjective etale atlas, proving the local presheaf quasi-compactness predicate.
The diagonal of p_i is a closed immersion; its arbitrary scheme tests remain closed immersions by base change. Hence the local presheaf separatedness predicate holds.

Use the specified cartesian squares to transport these two predicates to the local base changes of g. View T as its represented algebraic space and apply etale locality for the jointly surjective point cover.
